      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+[0-9]{8,15}$'
          example: '+61412345678'

          type: string
          maxLength: 255

          type: string
          format: date

## What I implemented

The rule: reject creating an owner when another owner has the same `lastName` **and** the same `address` (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace) with a **409**, unless the request sets `sharesHousehold: true`.

I followed the existing telephone-uniqueness pattern exactly, adding one step to the `POST /api/owners` OfficeFloor pipeline:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a `sharesHousehold` boolean to the `OwnerFields` schema so the generated `OwnerFieldsDto` exposes the request-only opt-out flag (documented as not persisted/returned).

2. **`CheckOwnerHouseholdUnique`** (new function) — reads the validated `@Val OwnerFieldsDto`; returns early when `sharesHousehold` is true; otherwise normalizes (`trim` → collapse whitespace runs → lower-case) the request's last name and address and compares against every existing owner, throwing `DuplicateOwnerHouseholdException` on a match.

3. **`DuplicateOwnerHouseholdException`** (checked, `extends Exception`) + **`DuplicateOwnerHouseholdExceptionHandler`** responding `409 CONFLICT`, wired via the escalation YAML `officefloor/escalation/…DuplicateOwnerHouseholdException.yml`.

4. **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted `checkHouseholdUnique` between `checkTelephoneUnique` and `build` (under `govern: [ transaction ]`), so a duplicate is a 409 before anything is persisted.

The three acceptance tests confirm the behavior: same last name + address → 409; different address → 2xx; and same last name + address with `sharesHousehold: true` → 2xx.

The rule: reject creating an owner when another owner has the same `lastName` **and** the same `address` (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace) with a **409**, unless the request sets `sharesHousehold: true`.

I followed the existing telephone-uniqueness pattern exactly, adding one step to the `POST /api/owners` OfficeFloor pipeline:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a `sharesHousehold` boolean to the `OwnerFields` schema so the generated `OwnerFieldsDto` exposes the request-only opt-out flag (documented as not persisted/returned).

2. **`CheckOwnerHouseholdUnique`** (new function) — reads the validated `@Val OwnerFieldsDto`; returns early when `sharesHousehold` is true; otherwise normalizes (`trim` → collapse whitespace runs → lower-case) the request's last name and address and compares against every existing owner, throwing `DuplicateOwnerHouseholdException` on a match.

3. **`DuplicateOwnerHouseholdException`** (checked, `extends Exception`) + **`DuplicateOwnerHouseholdExceptionHandler`** responding `409 CONFLICT`, wired via the escalation YAML `officefloor/escalation/…DuplicateOwnerHouseholdException.yml`.

4. **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted `checkHouseholdUnique` between `checkTelephoneUnique` and `build` (under `govern: [ transaction ]`), so a duplicate is a 409 before anything is persisted.

The three acceptance tests confirm the behavior: same last name + address → 409; different address → 2xx; and same last name + address with `sharesHousehold: true` → 2xx.
